# Mark Cuban Compared Nvidia to a Dot-Com-Era IPO Machine "Funding Everyone and Anyone." Here's What That Means for AI Stocks.

Motley Fool - 14 minutes ago

## Key Points [...] Cuban's warning is not a blanket argument against AI stocks. Large cloud providers and profitable AI chip and networking players can fund much of their spending from existing operations. A slowdown in data center construction could reduce their free cash flow, orders, or valuations, but it would not immediately threaten their ability to operate.

The warning matters most for companies that need regular outside funding to keep expanding. Specialized cloud operators face greater risk.

news.title: Feel the Burn? What the AI Capital Scoreboard Actually Measures
news.snippet: Capital raised and valuation are separate economic questions. A company that rai...
news.raw_snippet:
Capital raised and valuation are separate economic questions. A company that raised $1 billion and is marked at $50 billion does not “owe” investors $50 billion; investors hold an appreciated equity stake. Raising $10 billion is not economically equivalent to losing $10 billion.

The more interesting pattern

Once the misleading “payback” framing is stripped away, the chart reveals something more consequential: AI is increasingly separating into two very different capital regimes. [...] On the other side are application-layer and vertical companies. Cursor, ElevenLabs, Suno, Harvey, Perplexity and especially Midjourney convert comparatively modest external capital into substantial revenue far more quickly. Harvey’s additional $200 million financing in March at an $11 billion valuation is one illustration of how vertical AI can attract substantial valuations without needing frontier-lab-scale infrastructure financing. [...] sits at the efficient end. SpaceX announced a $60 billion all-stock acquisition in June, expected to close in the third quarter; describing the company as “on its way” into that structure is accurate. ElevenLabs had raised more than $781 million and surpassed $500 million ARR by May, producing a ratio near 1.6 years.
